Lesson · 25 min

Dropdowns, Protected Ranges, and Sharing Sheets

Keep shared sheets clean with dropdowns and checkboxes, protect formulas from accidental edits, leave notes and comments, and download a sheet as Excel or CSV.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Add a dropdown with Insert › Dropdown or Data › Data validation, and add checkboxes
  • ✓Protect a range so only you can edit it, and explain why protection is not a security measure
  • ✓Choose between a note and a comment
  • ✓Share a sheet and download it as Microsoft Excel or CSV

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Dropdowns and checkboxes

On the job

You manage the shared supply order sheet.

Four people add items to the monthly supply order. Categories are typed five different ways (cleaning, Cleaning, cleaning supplies), someone typed over the Total formulas last month, and Priya needs a copy in Excel for the accounting system.

Your task: Make the sheet hard to break, then share and download it.

  • Select the cells, then Insert › Dropdown (or Data › Data validation › Add rule, or right-click › Dropdown). The Data validation rules panel opens.
  • Under Criteria, keep Dropdown and type each option, clicking Add another item for more. Choose Dropdown from a range to use a list already in the sheet.
  • Advanced options: under If the data is invalid, entries that are not on the list are rejected by default; choose Show a warning to allow them with a warning. Display style can be Chip, Arrow, or Plain text.
  • Click Done. A dropdown appears in each cell.
  • Checkboxes: select the cells and choose Insert › Checkbox. Click a box to check it. You can use checkboxes with filters, charts, pivot tables, and functions.

Protecting formulas

  1. Select the cells, then Data › Protect sheets and ranges. A panel opens on the right.
  2. Click Add a sheet or range. Check the Range (or choose Sheet), and type a description.
  3. Click Set permissions. Choose Restrict who can edit this range and pick Only you (or Custom to add people), or choose Show a warning when editing this range.
  4. Click Done.
Protection prevents accidents; it is not a security measure. People who can view the sheet can still print, copy, paste, and export protected content. Share sheets only with people who should see what is in them.

Sharing and downloading

  • Share a sheet the same way as any file: Share at the top right, add people, pick Viewer, Commenter, or Editor.
  • File › Download › Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) downloads every sheet as an Excel workbook.
  • File › Download › Comma Separated Values (.csv) saves plain data for another system. A CSV file holds one sheet of data with no formatting, so open the sheet you need first.
  • File › Version history shows earlier versions. Restoring a spreadsheet version clears the cell-by-cell edit history for earlier changes; make a copy instead if you need to keep that history.

Knowledge Check

Check your understanding

You protected the Total column so only you can edit it. Can a coworker who can view the sheet copy those cells into another file?

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Finish your Budget Practice sheet.

  1. Add a dropdown to the Category column with three or four categories.
  2. Add a column named Paid with checkboxes.
  3. Protect the cells with your SUM and AVERAGE formulas so only you can edit them.
  4. Add a note to one cost explaining it.
  5. Download the spreadsheet as Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) and open it to check it.
Deliverable: Submit the .xlsx file to your instructor or course folder. No Google account? Complete the practice simulation and submit its results page.
